answer: A newcomer is issued one sealed vault holding a culture of a yeast strain, fed only on pollen from its own meadow plot. Each round the registry sends one whisper naming a nutrient; the holder feeds the culture and logs its growth curve, matched to its strain. The next nutrient follows from that curve and the holder's key; the sequence only advances in order. Each further identity needs another vault, strain, and meadow: $380 and 21 culture-days. 5,000 fakes would cost $1.9 million and 105,000 culture-days; one vault holds one strain, and a culture cannot be split without changing its curve.
